answer: Sealed Choreography Commitments: each agent must publish a signed plan of its next N actions, hashed with a per-agent secret key and a location-specific feature vector drawn from its current terrain cell (a karst fissure, meadow plot, or prism-marked survey stake). Plans are revealed only after execution; replays fail because the feature vector shifts. Duplicating an identity requires independently executing N distinct actions to produce a valid reveal, costing real compute and time per clone.
